cohort: Individuals delivering at more than 20 weeks of gestation at four U.S. hospitals from 2016 to 2019, excluding those with a personal history of VTE or thrombophilia, an antepartum diagnosis of VTE, or receiving therapeutic anticoagulation.
finding: Postpartum pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis did not reduce postpartum VTE but was associated with an increased risk for hospital readmission and wound complications.
mod_finding: Among individuals undergoing cesarean delivery, pharmacologic prophylaxis was associated with an increased risk for wound complications.
